newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnair fleet plans untouched by US merger.
newsitem.headline: Finnair fleet plans untouched by US merger.

text.p: Finnish airline Finnair Oy -- about to choose in 1997 the supplier for its fleet renewal -- said on Monday the announced merger of U.S. plane makers Boeing and McDonnel Douglas would not affect its plans.
"This merger decision will not affect our coming fleet renewal," Finnair chief spokesman Usko Maatta said by telephone.

Finnair has been a loyal buyer of McDonnel Douglas aircraft for the past 50 years. But it had said already that its choice next year of supplier for new medium-range, narrow-body planes for its European route network will be between Boeing and European manufacturer Airbus.
"McDonnel Douglas did not have a suitable aircraft in its production range," Maatta said.
In the first stage, Finnair's fleet renewal decision will be to replace 12 existing McDonnel Douglas DC-9 planes. "That decision will be made next year," Maatta said.
At a later stage, Finnair will renew more of its narrow-body fleet taking the total number of new planes to be purchased "up to 40," he added.
